designs.label: Tartan band
designs.layout: A broad band down the engine cover woven from crossing stripes over the second colour, with thin accent sett lines.
designs.after: Stewart SF01 (1997), the Stewart Racing tartan band

designs.label: Deck split
designs.layout: A level split, one colour per deck, with a double pinline on the seam (accent stripe plus a fine second line).
designs.after: Lotus 49B Gold Leaf (1968), red over white with gold

designs.label: Bordered stripe
designs.layout: One centre stripe with a keyline each side in the second colour and a body-colour gap between.

designs.label: Tricolour sweep
designs.layout: Three equal raked bands across the rear half: first colour, accent, second colour.
designs.after: Alpine A521 (2021) launch livery, flag stripes across the rear

designs.label: Spearhead
designs.layout: One arrow along the car: a broad head at the front of the cover and a level shaft behind it, keylined in the second colour.
designs.after: Brabham BT52 (1983), a two-colour block scheme drawn to read on TV
refs: Motor Sport: Peter Stevens on his liveries

rounds.changed: First round: five new cover layouts added to the SPINE TOP design picker (wrap placement so the art reaches both cover flanks), each shot on TLX in McLaren and Williams colours, front three-quarter and side. Before publishing, spearhead was reshaped from a raked wedge to a level-shafted arrow because it read like the tricolour on the flank. Known weak spots: on McLaren colours, bordered stripe and spearhead barely show because both pattern colours sit close to papaya, and spearhead vs bordered stripe is the least distinct pair (29.7% of the paint area). Round 2 target: give the stripe and arrow a contrast colour that is guaranteed to stand off the body.

Bryce: liveries are fine, so no fit investigation for this lane; instead, look at where else on the car decals and details could go. Added a map of the decal spots the car has today and eight candidate new spots, with real-F1 precedent and rough effort. No new captures this round (reuses round-1 frames).

existing: Rear-wing upper flap (sponsor band) and endplates (number)

proposed.label: Cockpit side
proposed.what: Driver name or three-letter code with a small flag, on the chassis side between the halo and the sidepod.
proposed.precedent: Every current car carries the driver's name or code here, next to the cockpit.
proposed.effort: Low: one flat decal quad like the existing sidepod panel decal, plus a new atlas region.

proposed.label: Halo top
proposed.what: A sponsor wordmark or colour band along the top of the halo.
proposed.precedent: McLaren sold its halo to Gandys at the 2018 Australian GP; Force India then ran Havaianas there.
proposed.effort: Medium: the halo is a tube, so the decal needs its own UV strip along it.

proposed.label: Sidepod top
proposed.what: The main sponsor along the sidepod's upper face, read from the chase camera and from above.
proposed.precedent: McLaren and Ferrari put their biggest sponsor here.
proposed.effort: Low: a strip on the pod's upper face, from the same pod stations as the side panel.

proposed.label: Floor edge
proposed.what: A long thin wordmark or accent line along the visible floor edge under the sidepod.
proposed.effort: Low: a strip quad on the floor edge.
proposed.status: not built: ride height moves the floor, so a decal would float or sink

proposed.label: Nose tip
proposed.what: Paint the nose tip a contrast colour, or carry a small mark there.
proposed.precedent: 2026 cars paint the tip deliberately (Alpine dark blue, Red Bull red), per the 2026 livery reference note.
proposed.effort: Low: a colour zone on the existing nose mesh; no new atlas region.
